segments.text: This is another in a series of lectures by Swami H. V. Rupaji at his ashram on July 12, 1975.
This will be a continuation of the in-commentary on Shiva Sutra V. Marshani.
The previous Sutra you have, you have to understand that previous Sutra explained the limited powers of Yoga, yogic powers.
Now, in the 21st he will explain unlimited yogic powers. Those were limited yogic powers.
Bhutasandana, Bhutopratakto, Vishu Sangatya. Yadatu, Mithi, Siddhir, Anabhila, Shen.
And he does not put his desire for these limited powers and tries to attain the knowledge of universal being.
Then, for such a yogi, Shuddha Vidyodaya, Chakraya, Shattu, Siddhi, pure knowledge rises.
And by that, he becomes Chakraeshwara. He becomes the master of the universal world, just like Lord Krishna did.
He utilized his powers in universal way, not in limited way. Lord Krishna, for instance, take his appearance in Vishu Rupa Darshan.
That was the greatest yogic power. And so on, many like those powers, he utilized.
And it was due to his being master on check, universal being. He had not limitedness as some yogi will tell you,
you will get through your examination with good success, good remarks. These powers are called limited powers.
You want rain, rainfall, it will come, that power is unlimited power. That is universal power.
You want earthquake to happen, that is universal power. You want destruction of the whole universe, that is universal power.
You want rise and happiness for the universe, that is universal power. But there is no individuality in the background that is universal power.
That is Chakrayeshwara. That is becoming master on checkra, Shakti-chakra. And that rises by the rise of pure knowledge, Shuddha Vidyodaya.
Vaisyath-myapratha-vanchaya, Yadav-Shaktim-Sandhati, when he concentrates or contemplates his energy of will for attaining the universal state of being,
then he finds amyav-sarvam, Yadav-Shuddha Vidyaya. This pure knowledge comes in him, that I am the whole universe. I am not only body. I am one with universe.

Then Vaisyath-myapratha-shakti-chakrayeshwara-surupa-mahesharyam-asya-siddhati. Then this glory of Maheshara is obtained by that sadhaka, that yogi, by which he becomes the master of universal beings.
It is also quoted in Sachanda, Tasmāt-sāt-parā Vidyaya, Yasmāt-anyā-niv-navid-diti.
This is the supreme knowledge, but he achieves. And there is no other better knowledge than that. This is the only supreme knowledge.

Because Vindhate-hyatra-yugupat-sārvagyāda-guna-an-parān. Parān-sārvagyāda-guna. He obtains, Vindhate, he attains, Yugupat simultaneously, Parān-supreme-sārvagyāda-guna, the glories of all knowledge and all action.
This is supreme knowledge. This is said to be supreme knowledge of Yugupat-sārvagyāda-guna. And what is knowledge?
In addition, he explains more for this supreme knowledge. Veda-nā-nā-nā-vid-dharma-sya-paramāt-māt-bho-dana-anā-vid-dharma-sya.
When eternal aspects of Lord Shiva, eternal aspect, eternal aspect is the energy of Sātantra.
Then that energy of Sātantra, which is eternal aspect of Lord Shiva, is known. Parāmāt-māt-bho-dana and supreme eye consciousness is also in his knowledge.
Vagyana-aparamāt-māt-bho-dā, absin's of supreme knowledge. Absin's of that is kept away. Absin's of aparamāt-māt-māt-māt mean, absin's of supreme consciousness is kept away.
This is why it is called knowledge, the pure knowledge, Shuddha Vidya.
Tatrastha you should establish, you should be established in that supreme knowledge and
you should expose in your own nature the supreme light of the supreme being.
Then that supreme light takes place, it is exposed, you become one with that supreme light.
Tatrastha Shuddha amrajit, or you become one with Lord Shiva.
This is narrated in Spanda in this shloka.
Vedereke, Sravarthhan, Yadavya, Vyapya with this state, when he pervets the whole universe,
including his individual being, then what is to be said for him?
What is to be explained or spoken for him?
Sai Mewa Ubotsita, he understands this state, his state, by himself.
Yadavthu, Sathma Ramata, Mewa, Hchati, Tada, I sayer.
When on the contrary, some yogis are not like this.
They don't want to create these universal powers, yogic powers.
Just like Rama did.
So Rama, Abdashiratha, he had no universal power, but he was above that.
He didn't utilize any universal power, he utilized his weapons, his strength, his energy.
But no universal power, he had no universal power.
He didn't like to have universal power, because his mind was focused in his own nature.
